text:
What is:
card_val_ran1 in npccard1 != card_val_ran2 in npccard2

meant to check?
It’s called a “chained comparison” and it’s short for:
(card_val_ran1 in npccard1) and (npccard1 != card_val_ran2) and (card_val_ran2 in npccard2)

A simpler example is:
a == b == c

which is short for:
(a == b) and (b == c)

Did you mean and instead of != (not equal), or are you checking whether only one of:
card_val_ran1 in npccard1

and
card_val_ran2 in npccard2

is true?
(That would have to be written:
(card_val_ran1 in npccard1) != (card_val_ran2 in npccard2)

)
